newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokesman Kochen Kubosch briefed on Tuesday's Industry Council. Kubosch said the exchange of views would focus on recent actions undertaken in the field of the information society. He also said the ministers of the central and eastern European countries (CEEC) would join for a one hour meeting and lunch in order to discuss pilot actions between the EU and CEEC.

In answer to a question, spokesman Josep Coll i Carbo said the EU had an important role to play in the Middle East both from an economic and political point of view. Coll i Carbo insisted that EU's political voice was appreciated and requested.

On Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring's visit to the Middle East, Coll i Cabro said it was necessary for the EU to be on the spot very quickly. Coll i Carbo also confirmed a visit by a troika of EU-ministers to the region after Spring's visit.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/892: Commission grants aid for Chernobyl victims and fight against diptheria in Ukraine.
- IP/96/893: 1996 High level consultations on the environment between the European Commission and the government of the United States.
- IP/96/895: "Cities and regions info way to Europe" conference in Barcelona.
- IP/96/896: Commission welcomes closer links with Korea.
- Speech/96/237: Speech by Commissioner Bjerregaard at the second European conference on sustainable cities and towns.
- Speech/96/238: Speech by Commissioner Flynn on the launch of the fourth action programme for equal opportunities - Mechanisms for mainstreaming.
- Memo/96/94: A regulatory framework for a single market information society services.
